δύ εται ὁ ἥλιο ἐπὶ τοὺ προφήτα ὑμῶν με ημβρία , οὕτως καὶ δύει ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς
ἁμαρτάνοντας, οὐ χαριζόμενος αὐτοῖς ἔτι ἁμαρτάνουσι τὴν ἰδίαν ἀνατολήν.
ἐντέλλεται οὖν ἡμῖν ὁ Παῦλος μὴ ποιῆσαι τοιαῦτα κατὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ὡς ἐπιδῦναι ἡμῖν
τὸν ἥλιον καὶ γενέσθαι ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν νύκτα. 20 Eph. iv27 [μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον
τῷ διαβόλῳ.] [Ὠριγένης δέ φησιν] ὅμοιον τοῦτό ἐστι τῷ ἐν τῷ Ἐκκλησιαστῇ
εἰρημένῳ, ἐὰν πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐξου ιά ζοντο ἀναβῇ ἐπί ε τόπον ου μὴ ἀφῇ , ὅτι ἴαμα
καταπαύ ει ἁμαρτία μεγάλα . τόπον δὲ δίδομεν τῷ διαβόλῳ ἢ τῷ ἐξου ιάζοντι
πνεύματι ἀναβάντι ἐφ' ἡμᾶς, ὅτε οὐ πεπλήρωται ἡμῶν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἁγίων
μαθημάτων ἢ τῆς σωτηρίου πίστεως καὶ λογισμῶν διαφερόντων καὶ
συμβουλευόντων ἡμῖν τὰ ἄριστα· κατὰ γὰρ τὸν πατέρα Ἰωάννου Ζαχαρίαν ἐπὶ τὰ
κλίματα τῆ ψυχῆ ἐπι κηνοῖ ὁ Σατανᾶ , καὶ αἱ τοιαίδε συγκαταθέσεις τοῖς χείροσι καὶ
ῥοπαὶ ἐπὶ τὰς συγκαταθέσεις προκαλοῦνται τὸν διάβολον εἰσελθεῖν ἡμῶν εἰς τὰς
ψυχάς. καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα γοῦν γέγραπται τοῦ προδότου, πρότερον μὲν τοῦ διαβόλου
ἤδη βεβληκότο εἰ τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα παραδῷ αὐτὸν Ἰούδα Σίμωνο Ἰ καριώτη , μετὰ
δὲ ταῦτα ὅτι μετὰ τὸ ψωμίον εἰ ῆλθεν εἰ ἐκεῖνον ὁ Σατανᾶ · ὡς εἰ, βεβληκότο τοῦ
διαβόλου εἰ τὴν καρδίαν Ἰούδα ἵνα παραδῷ τὸν Κύριον, πρὸς τὸ βληθὲν στὰς ὁ
Ἰούδας ἦν, οὐκ ἂν ὕστερον εὑρήκει τόπον εἰς αὐτὸν εἰ ελθεῖν ὁ Σατανᾶ . [ iv 28] ὁ
κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος τὸ ἀγαθὸν ταῖς
χερσίν, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι. ἐπείπερ ἐν ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις
ἀναστρεφόμενοι προφάσει τοῦ πορισμοῦ τῶν ἐπιτηδείων καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν
πεπιστευκέναι νομιζομένων, κἂν δοκῶσι καθαρεύειν ἀπὸ εἰδωλολατρείας καὶ πάσης
πορνείας, οὐκ εὐκόλως ἀφίστανται τοῦ κλέπτειν ἐν τῷ ὠνεῖσθαι καὶ πιπράσκειν καὶ
συμπραγμα τεύεσθαί τισι, διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ὤκνησεν, ὡς ἔτι κλεπτόντων (καὶ ταῦτα ἐν
Ἐφέσῳ) τινῶν, οἱονεὶ ἐλέγξαι ὡς εἰδὼς τοὺς τοιούτους· τὸν δὲ δίκαιον πορισμὸν
δηλοῖ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐργαζόμενος τὸ ἀγαθόν, τῶν μὲν ἀδίκως ποριζόντων οὐ τὸ ἀγαθὸν
ἀλλὰ τὸ πονηρὸν ἐργαζομένων, τῶν δὲ μετ' εὐλαβείας περιποιούντων αὐτοῖς τὰ
ἀναγκαῖα καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργαζομένων. 21 Eph. iv29 [πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ
τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω ἀλλ' εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας
ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.] [Ὠριγένης φησίν] ἀγαθὸς λόγος ἐστὶ πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν
τῆς χρείας διδοὺς χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν ὁ διδασκαλικὸς καὶ ἐπ' ἀρετὴν μὲν
προτρεπτικὸς κακίας δὲ ἀποστερητικός· σαπρὸς δέ, ὁ συναύξων τὴν κακίαν καὶ
ἐρεθίζων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρονα. [ iv 30] καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ
ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως. εἴπερ ἡ λύπη πάθος ἐστί, καὶ καλῶς
ἀποδίδοται περὶ αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐστὶ «δόξα πρόσφατος κακοῦ παρουσίας ἐφ' ᾧ καθήκει
συστέλλεσθαι,» οὔτε δὲ δοξάζει τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα οὔτε (ἵνα δοθῇ δοξάζειν) δοξάζει τὸ
κακὸν αὐτῷ παρεῖναι, οὐ λυπήσεται τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. μήποτ' οὖν, τὸ ὅσον ἐφ' ἡμῖν,
τάδε πράττοντες λυποῦμεν τὸ
pass_a_gloss: the sun sets on your prophets at midday, so also it sets on all who sin, no longer granting them its own rising while they still sin. Paul therefore commands us not to do such things in anger that the sun should set on us and night come about in our souls. Do not give place to the devil. Origen says this is like what is said in Ecclesiastes: if the spirit of the one who has authority rises upon you, do not leave your place, because healing will put a great sin to rest. We give place to the devil or to the ruling spirit that has risen upon us when our governing part is not filled with holy teachings or saving faith and with distinguishing reasonings that counsel us the best things. For according to Zechariah, father of John, Satan pitches tent upon the regions of the soul, and such assents to the worse and inclinations toward assents call the devil to enter our souls. And of Judas the traitor it is written that first the devil had already cast into his heart that Judas son of Simon Iscariot should betray him, and after this that after the morsel Satan entered into him; so that if, when the devil had cast into Judas's heart to betray the Lord, Judas had stood against what was cast, Satan would not later have found place to enter him. Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labor, working the good with his hands, that he may have to give to the one in need. Since in the dealings of life many who are thought to have believed, even if they seem clean from idolatry and all fornication, do not easily leave off stealing in buying and selling and doing business with some, on the pretext of procuring necessities—for this reason he did not hesitate, as if some were still stealing (and that in Ephesus), to rebuke as knowing such people. Just provision is shown by working the good: those who provide unjustly work not the good but the evil, while those who with reverence secure necessities for themselves in this also work the good. Let no rotten word go out of your mouth, but if any is good for building up the need, that it may give grace to those who hear. A good word for building the need, giving grace to hearers, is the teaching word that exhorts toward virtue and strips away vice; rotten is what increases vice and stirs toward worse things. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for a day of redemption. If grief is a passion, and it is well defined as a fresh opinion of the presence of evil at which it is fitting to contract, and the Holy Spirit neither forms opinions nor (even if one grants that it forms opinions) forms the opinion that evil is present to it, the Holy Spirit will not be grieved. Perhaps then, as far as it lies with us, by doing such things we grieve the Holy Spirit of God? And the Lord says in Ezekiel, In all these you grieved me. What we have often said about anger and wrath and sleep and anthropopathic language is useful also for the word about not grieving the Holy Spirit of God. We were sealed with the Holy Spirit so that, receiving the imprint of the Holy Spirit, the sealer remaining undivided, taking the imprints of the Holy Spirit we may become holy, and the spirit of the human being in each of us that is in us may become holy—and I think also the soul. The one sealed is sealed with the Holy Spirit, but God is the one who seals. Everyone who from believing God has a seal that God is true is sealed by the Father with the Holy Spirit; and he is sealed so that, keeping the seal and showing it unbroken on the day of redemption, he may be numbered with those being redeemed. Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and blasphemy be taken away from you, with all malice. Origen says: some thought anger a generic passion and ranked it under desire as genus; and they gave such a definition of anger: Anger is desire of punishment of the one who seems to have wronged improperly. Listing many species of anger, they rank with them bitterness as anger hard to receive or bursting out at once (and they say hard to receive is taken—
pass_b_english: Just as the sun sets on your prophets at midday, it sets on every sinner and no longer grants its rising while they keep sinning. Paul therefore orders us not to act in anger so that this sun sets on us and night fills our souls.

[[Ephesians 4:27 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:27]] "Do not give place to the devil." Origen links this with Ecclesiastes: if a ruling spirit rises over you, do not leave your place, for healing stops a great sin. We give the devil—or that ruling spirit—room when the governing part is empty of holy teaching, saving faith, and discerning thoughts that counsel what is best. As with Zechariah, Satan camps on the soul's regions; assents to worse things invite him in. Judas shows the pattern: first the devil cast betrayal into his heart; later, after the morsel, Satan entered. Had Judas resisted the first cast, Satan would have found no later place.

[[Ephesians 4:28 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:28]] "Let the thief steal no more, but rather labor, working the good with his hands, so he may share with the one in need." Even among those thought believers—clean, it seems, of idolatry and fornication—buying, selling, and trade often hide theft under the excuse of getting necessities. So Paul does not shrink from rebuking thieves still at work in Ephesus. "Working the good" marks just provision: unjust gain works evil; reverent securing of necessities works the good.

[[Ephesians 4:29 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:29]] "Let no rotten word leave your mouth, but only what is good for needed building-up, that it may give grace to hearers." The good word teaches, urges virtue, and strips vice. The rotten word feeds vice and pushes toward worse.

[[Ephesians 4:30 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:30]] "Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for a day of redemption." Strictly, grief is a passion—a fresh judgment that evil is present and one should contract. The Spirit does not form such judgments, so in that sense it is not grieved. Yet as far as it depends on us, by doing these things we grieve God's Holy Spirit; the Lord says in Ezekiel, "In all these you grieved me." Our earlier notes on anger, wrath, sleep, and God-spoken human feelings help here too.

Sealing with the Spirit gives us its imprint while the Sealer stays undivided, so we become holy—and our human spirit, and I think the soul too. God seals; the Spirit is the seal. Everyone who believes God true receives that seal from the Father, to keep it unbroken until the day of redemption and be counted among the redeemed.

[[Ephesians 4:31 >> Bible:Ephesians 4:31]] "Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and blasphemy be removed from you, with all malice." Some make anger a species under desire: desire to punish one who seems to have wronged you wrongly. Among its forms they place bitterness as anger hard for others to receive, or as anger that bursts out at once—continued in the next section.
